notes.text: (1) Psalm xciv. 12; Numbers xii. 8. (2) John viii. 25 (Vulg.).

verses.text: Happy is the man whom Truth by itself doth teach, not by figures and transient words, but as it is in itself.(1) Our own judgment and feelings often deceive us, and we discern but little of the truth.
verses.modernizedText: Happy is the person whom Truth itself teaches, not by figures and passing words, but as it is in itself.(1) Our own judgment and feelings often deceive us, and we discern little of the truth.

verses.text: What doth it profit to argue about hidden and dark things, concerning which we shall not be even reproved in the judgment, because we knew them not?
verses.modernizedText: What good is it to argue about hidden and obscure things, for ignorance of which we will not even be reproved at the judgment?

verses.text: Oh, grievous folly, to neglect the things which are profitable and necessary, and to give our minds to things which are curious and hurtful!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, what grievous folly to neglect the things that are profitable and necessary and set our minds on things that are curious and harmful!

verses.text: Having eyes, we see not.
verses.modernizedText: Having eyes, we do not see.

verses.text: And what have we to do with talk about genus and species!
verses.modernizedText: And what have we to do with talk about genus and species!

verses.text: He to whom the Eternal Word speaketh is free from multiplied questionings.
verses.modernizedText: The person to whom the Eternal Word speaks is free from many questions.

verses.text: From this One Word are all things, and all things speak of Him; and this is the Beginning which also speaketh unto us.(2) No man without Him understandeth or rightly judgeth.
verses.modernizedText: From this One Word are all things, and all things speak of Him; and this is the Beginning who also speaks to us.(2) No one without Him understands or judges rightly.

verses.text: The man to whom all things are one, who bringeth all things to one, who seeth all things in one, he is able to remain steadfast of spirit, and at rest in God.
verses.modernizedText: The person to whom all things are one, who brings all things to one, who sees all things in one, is able to remain steadfast in spirit and at rest in God.

verses.text: O God, who art the Truth, make me one with Thee in everlasting love.
verses.modernizedText: O God, who are the Truth, make me one with You in everlasting love.

verses.text: It wearieth me oftentimes to read and listen to many things; in Thee is all that I wish for and desire.
verses.modernizedText: It often wearies me to read and listen to many things; in You is all that I wish for and desire.

verses.text: Let all the doctors hold their peace; let all creation keep silence before Thee: speak Thou alone to me.
verses.modernizedText: Let all the doctors hold their peace; let all creation keep silence before You: speak to me, You alone.

verses.text: The more a man hath unity and simplicity in himself, the more things and the deeper things he understandeth; and that without labour, because he receiveth the light of understanding from above.
verses.modernizedText: The more unity and simplicity a person has within himself, the more things and the deeper things he understands, and that without labor, because he receives the light of understanding from above.

verses.text: The spirit which is pure, sincere, and steadfast, is not distracted though it hath many works to do, because it doth all things to the honour of God, and striveth to be free from all thoughts of self-seeking.
verses.modernizedText: A spirit that is pure, sincere, and steadfast is not distracted even when it has many works to do, because it does all things to the honor of God and strives to be free from all self-seeking thoughts.

verses.text: Who is so full of hindrance and annoyance to thee as thine own undisciplined heart?
verses.modernizedText: Who is so full of hindrance and annoyance to you as your own undisciplined heart?

verses.text: A man who is good and devout arrangeth beforehand within his own heart the works which he hath to do abroad; and so is not drawn away by the desires of his evil will, but subjecteth everything to the judgment of right reason.
verses.modernizedText: A good and devout person arranges beforehand within his own heart the works he has to do outwardly; and so he is not drawn away by the desires of his evil will, but subjects everything to the judgment of right reason.

verses.text: Who hath a harder battle to fight than he who striveth for self-mastery?
verses.modernizedText: Who has a harder battle to fight than the person who strives for self-mastery?

verses.text: And this should be our endeavour, even to master self, and thus daily to grow stronger than self, and go on unto perfection.
verses.modernizedText: And this should be our endeavor: to master ourselves and so grow stronger than ourselves daily and go on to perfection.

verses.text: All perfection hath some imperfection joined to it in this life, and all our power of sight is not without some darkness.
verses.modernizedText: All perfection in this life has some imperfection joined to it, and all our power of sight is not without some darkness.

verses.text: A lowly knowledge of thyself is a surer way to God than the deep searching of man’s learning.
verses.modernizedText: A humble knowledge of yourself is a surer way to God than a deep search into human learning.

verses.text: Not that learning is to be blamed, nor the taking account of anything that is good; but a good conscience and a holy life is better than all.
verses.modernizedText: Not that learning is to be blamed, nor the taking account of anything that is good; but a good conscience and a holy life are better than all.

verses.text: And because many seek knowledge rather than good living, therefore they go astray, and bear little or no fruit.
verses.modernizedText: And because many seek knowledge rather than good living, they go astray and bear little or no fruit.

verses.text: O if they would give that diligence to the rooting out of vice and the planting of virtue which they give unto vain questionings: there had not been so many evil doings and stumbling-blocks among the laity, nor such ill living among houses of religion.
verses.modernizedText: Oh, if they gave the diligence to rooting out vice and planting virtue that they give to vain questions, there would not have been so many evil deeds and stumbling blocks among the laity, nor such evil living in religious houses.

verses.text: Of a surety, at the Day of Judgment it will be demanded of us, not what we have read, but what we have done; not how well we have spoken, but how holily we have lived.
verses.modernizedText: Certainly, at the Day of Judgment we will be asked not what we have read, but what we have done; not how well we have spoken, but how holy a life we have lived.

verses.text: Tell me, where now are all those masters and teachers, whom thou knewest well, whilst they were yet with you, and flourished in learning?
verses.modernizedText: Tell me, where now are all those masters and teachers whom you knew well while they were still with you and flourished in learning?

verses.text: Their stalls are now filled by others, who perhaps never have one thought concerning them.
verses.modernizedText: Their places are now filled by others, who perhaps never give them a thought.

verses.text: Whilst they lived they seemed to be somewhat, but now no one speaks of them.
verses.modernizedText: While they lived they seemed to be something, but now no one speaks of them.

verses.text: Oh how quickly passeth the glory of the world away!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, how quickly the glory of the world passes away!

verses.text: Would that their life and knowledge had agreed together!
verses.modernizedText: If only their life and knowledge had agreed with each other!

verses.text: For then would they have read and inquired unto good purpose.
verses.modernizedText: For then they would have read and inquired to good purpose.

verses.text: How many perish through empty learning in this world, who care little for serving God.
verses.modernizedText: How many perish through empty learning in this world, caring little for serving God.

verses.text: And because they love to be great more than to be humble, therefore they “have become vain in their imaginations.”
verses.modernizedText: And because they love to be great more than to be humble, they “have become vain in their imaginations.”

verses.text: He only is truly great, who hath great charity.
verses.modernizedText: Only the person who has great charity is truly great.

verses.text: He is truly great who deemeth himself small, and counteth all height of honour as nothing.
verses.modernizedText: The person who considers himself small and counts all heights of honor as nothing is truly great.

verses.text: He is the truly wise man, who counteth all earthly things as dung that he may win Christ.
verses.modernizedText: The truly wise person counts all earthly things as dung so that he may win Christ.

verses.text: And he is the truly learned man, who doeth the will of God, and forsaketh his own will.
verses.modernizedText: And the truly learned person does the will of God and forsakes his own will.
